thread:
maya (Product): quick sync — we're seeing a bunch of confusion in the console about saved queries / views for routes vs models. folks expect per-route defaults, but saved queries currently live in a global bucket. can we discuss options?

evan (UX): +1, heard this in user interviews. current flow: open route -> open analytics -> reapply filters every time. we should let teams pin a default view per-route (filters + time range + model selection). :thumbsup:

sanjay (Eng): curious about backend shape — do we treat saved views as namespaced resources or as global objects with scope metadata? my vote: namespaced endpoints, e.g. GET /routes/{route_id}/views and GET /models/{model_id}/views, with a fallback global GET /views?scope=global

jia (Data): telemetry perspective — our event schema includes route_id and model_id, so query scoping is doable. two caveats: (1) some older events don't have model_id for early routes, (2) query performance for large orgs — need pagination and precomputed aggregates for charts.

evan (UX): also want to support "route-level quick presets" where you can save "Top latency by user-agent" and make it discoverable when devs open that route. visual affordance: small dropdown near route title: "view: <preset>"

leo (Platform): backend constraints: if we add per-route pins, we need to enforce RBAC and sharing semantics. do pinned defaults inherit route ACLs? e.g., org vs team vs private views. recommend metadata: {"scope":"route|model|org|user","owner_id":"...","shared_with":[]}. also we should avoid creating N views per route by autosaving transient presets — require explicit save.

sanjay (Eng): implementation sketch:

```
POST /routes/{route_id}/views
body: {
  "name": "High-latency-by-region",
  "filters": { "latency_ms": ">200", "region": "eu-west" },
  "visualization": "timeseries",
  "scope": "route",
  "is_default": true
}
```

GET /routes/{route_id}/views -> returns all route-scoped + inherited org-scoped views (ordered by default flag and recency).

tess (PM): migration question — we have ~1200 global saved queries. if we introduce route scope, what's the UX to map existing ones? auto-suggest mappings based on filter predicates (if filters reference single route or model) and ask user to confirm. fallback: keep as global.

jia (Data): about aggregates — suggest we precompute common metric slices (latency p50/p95, token-cost, error-rate) per route daily/hourly. the console should query these aggregates for quick rendering and fall back to raw events for ad-hoc queries.

evan (UX): small but important: when someone switches model inside a route, the view should remember which model was last selected for that route (sticky) — separate from saved views. this avoids accidental comparing across incompatible models.

leo (Platform): rollout visibility tie-in: when route is part of a canary rollout, console should surface which view/filters were recorded during the rollout window. maybe attach rollout_id to analytics export so users can filter by rollout.

sanjay (Eng): authorization & caching notes: route-scoped views should be cached keyed by route_id and user-perms; when ACL changes, invalidate. also think about rate limits for orgs with many routes — we'll add a summary endpoint: GET /routes/{route_id}/views/summary that returns counts and default id only.

maya (Product): action items: 1) tech design doc for namespaced views (sanjay + leo) 2) UX mockups for per-route pin + sticky model (evan) 3) migration plan for global queries (tess + jia) — can we aim for a short RFC by EOW?

deploy-bot: deploy starting to channel "console" (deploy/2026-03-18T14:20Z) :rocket:

maya (Product): ok — flagged owners in thread. one open question: should saved views include the model variant/quantization setting (so the view is reproducible)? i lean yes. thoughts?

sanjay (Eng): yes include model_ref + model_variant + quantization_profile as optional fields. otherwise you can't reproduce charts that rely on model-specific telemetry (e.g., tokenization counts).

jia (Data): agree. but we should treat variant as filter metadata, not as a hard binding — views can be set to "fixed variant" or "follow route default".

evan (UX): will prototype 2 small flows: "pin default view" and "save named view" with scope selector (Private / Team / Route / Org). will post frames later today.

maya (Product): perfect. thanks everyone. i'll draft owner-facing acceptance criteria for the RFC: must cover API contract, RBAC, migration UX, stats precompute plan, and console mockups.

leo (Platform): one last ops note: for Dedicated/private customers we should honor their network egress and opt-out of our aggregate export jobs unless they enable telemetry export. add to RFC.

maya (Product): added. closing loop — will convert this thread into an RFC ticket and ping owners. :white_check_mark:
